name: CoolSculpting (cryolipolysis)

lead: CoolSculpting (cryolipolysis) thins a stubborn local fat layer, including under the chin and along the jawline, for a slimmer contour without surgery. The FDA has cleared it for areas including the submental area, jawline, arms, flanks, abdomen and thighs.

An applicator cools the fat to a temperature that injures fat cells while sparing the skin, and the body clears the damaged cells over the following weeks. A 2015 review of 19 studies found skinfold thickness reductions of 10.3 to 28.5 percent with high satisfaction, and a 2023 review of 18 studies reported ultrasound-measured reductions of 2.0 to 5.1 mm. The effect is local and modest, and is not weight loss. Facial use beyond cleared areas and ideas about brown-fat conversion are forum theories.

paras: Treatment is done in a clinic, with an applicator held on the area for a session lasting about an hour. Results appear gradually over weeks to a few months, and some people have additional sessions on the same area. It is commonly used by people already near their goal weight who want to refine a specific spot.

Redness, numbness, swelling, bruising and mild pain are common and usually resolve within weeks. Paradoxical adipose hyperplasia, where the treated fat enlarges, has been reported at roughly 0.12 to 1.0 percent and can require liposuction or abdominoplasty to correct.

chain: Local fat layer thins over weeks
angle.text: Used to thin stubborn local fat, including under the chin and along the jawline, for a sharper contour. Cold damages targeted fat cells and the layer thins over weeks; reviews show modest local reductions in cleared body areas.

lead: Cryolipolysis, often called fat freezing, is a non-invasive procedure that uses controlled cooling of subcutaneous fat for localized fat reduction. The term is frequently used interchangeably with the brand name CoolSculpting, introduced in the United States in 2010 by Zeltiq Aesthetics and acquired by Allergan Aesthetics in 2017 [1]. The FDA has cleared it for several body areas including the submental area, jawline, arms, flanks, abdomen and thighs [1].

Systematic reviews have reported moderate effectiveness. A 2015 review of 19 studies found skinfold thickness reductions of 10.3 to 28.5 percent with high patient satisfaction, and a 2023 review of 18 studies reported ultrasound-measured fat reductions of 2.0 to 5.1 mm and judged the treatment safe but modestly effective, with low-quality data [1]. Reviews in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery and elsewhere address efficacy, methods and complications [2][3].
On looksmax.org the procedure has been described as a way to cause local fat loss, including a thread proposing it for facial fat pockets [4].
infobox: CoolSculpting (Zeltiq, acquired by Allergan Aesthetics in 2017) [1]
Submental, jawline, arms, lumbar rolls, flanks, abdomen, thighs, under buttocks [1]
2.0 to 5.1 mm by ultrasound in a 2023 review [1]
Paradoxical adipose hyperplasia, about 0.12 to 1.0 percent [1]

paras: Cryolipolysis applies controlled cold to a section of tissue. A pig-model study published in Dermatologic Surgery in 2009 examined whether controlled cooling could selectively damage subcutaneous fat without injuring overlying skin and surrounding structures [5]. A review in Lasers in Surgery and Medicine summarized the preclinical and clinical evidence on mechanism, efficacy and safety [6].
A human study in Aesthetic Plastic Surgery also examined whether the treatment affects local sensory function or nerve fibers [7].

Wikipedia summarizes reviews reporting skinfold reductions of 10.3 to 28.5 percent (2015, 19 studies) and ultrasound fat-thickness reductions of 2.0 to 5.1 mm (2023, 18 studies), with the latter noting low data quality [1]. Studies have also used three-dimensional volumetric measurement of fat loss [8] and have tested the treatment on submental fat [9]. A review of noninvasive subcutaneous fat reduction compared cryolipolysis with other methods [10].

Common effects include redness, numbness, swelling, bruising and mild pain, usually resolving within weeks. Paradoxical adipose hyperplasia (PAH), in which the treated fat enlarges, has been reported in about 0.12 to 1.0 percent of treatments and has been treated with liposuction or abdominoplasty [1]. Studies of safety, tolerance and patient satisfaction have been published [11].

Pig-model results were published in 2009 [5], followed by early human efficacy studies [7]. Zeltiq introduced CoolSculpting in the US in 2010 and Allergan Aesthetics acquired it in 2017 [1]. A 2013 article gave a broad overview of clinical and commercial experience with the device [12].

Human studies include a systematic review of clinical data on efficacy and safety [2], a literature review [6], studies of submental fat [9], volumetric quantification of fat loss [8], and a study of effects on peripheral nerves [7]. Registered trials include one of cryolipolysis combined with aerobic exercise for abdominal fat [13] and one comparing ultrasound lipolysis with cryolipolysis on lipid profile in centrally obese men [14]. Wikipedia describes the evidence overall as moderate in effect, with low data quality in the most recent review [1].

A looksmax.org thread presents fat freezing as a local fat-loss method, and replies ask whether it could reduce fat under the cheekbones [4]. The posts are anecdotal and stated in the posters' own terms; they are not supported by the clinical literature on facial application beyond the submental region cleared by the FDA [1][9].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, cryolipolysis is discussed as a possible way to remove facial or submental fat locally, with members debating whether it suits younger men with low body fat [4].

claims.claim: Freezing fat is a legitimate way to get local fat loss, even from the face.
Cold causes white fat to convert to brown fat that burns off.

timeline.event: Pig-model study and first human efficacy and nerve-safety studies of cryolipolysis published [5][7].
